programme.displayName: RDS, EC2, and Application Load Balancer Follow Along
programme.subtitle: Build a beginner three-tier SAA-C03 practice architecture in Europe (London): internet → Application Load Balancer → EC2 → private RDS for MySQL.
programme.description: Create every resource from the beginning in eu-west-2: a dedicated training identity, a six-subnet VPC, internet and NAT routing, least-privilege security groups, private EC2 web targets behind an Application Load Balancer, and a private RDS for MySQL DB instance. Validate availability, monitoring, backups, controlled failures, and core AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Associate SAA-C03 architecture choices.
programme.learningOutcome: Build, verify, monitor, troubleshoot, and clean up an internet-facing Application Load Balancer that routes HTTP traffic to private EC2 web targets while a private RDS for MySQL DB instance accepts MySQL traffic only from the EC2 security group. Recognize SAA-C03 requirements for ALB, private subnets, NAT gateways, security-group references, Multi-AZ, read replicas, Auto Scaling, RDS Proxy, Aurora, and Network Load Balancer.

phases.title: Secure account access and AWS CLI setup
phases.description: Protect the account root user, create the dedicated training identity, create narrowly scoped training permissions, and configure the named CLI profile.

phases.title: Create the complete multi-tier VPC
phases.description: Create the dedicated VPC, six subnets in two Availability Zones, an internet gateway, public and private route tables, and a NAT gateway path.

phases.title: Create network access controls and managed instance access
phases.description: Create the ALB, web, and RDS security-group chain, then prepare Session Manager access without opening SSH.

phases.title: Deploy private web targets and an Application Load Balancer
phases.description: Launch private EC2 web servers, configure the target group, create the ALB and listener, and verify healthy browser traffic.

phases.title: Create and connect to private RDS for MySQL
phases.description: Create the DB subnet group and private DB instance, record its endpoint, and verify EC2-to-RDS connectivity.

phases.title: Resilience, observability, backups, and controlled troubleshooting
phases.description: Add a second target, inspect metrics, create an alarm and manual snapshot, practice reversible failures, and review SAA-C03 choices.

phases.title: Remove the complete training environment
phases.description: Delete only the named resources in safe reverse-dependency order and verify that chargeable resources are gone.

tasks.title: Protect the root user and create the training IAM user
tasks.goal: Use the root user only for account-only tasks, then create the non-root training user fa-rds-alb-ec2-lab-user.
tasks.whyItMatters: The root user has unrestricted account access and must not be used for normal administration. SAA-C03 wording such as least privilege, temporary credentials, and avoid root should lead you to IAM roles, federated access, and scoped permissions.

consoleSteps.title: Create the dedicated training user
consoleSteps.instruction: ☐ Sign in with the root user only if no administrator exists.

instructions.text: ☐ Sign in with the root user only if no administrator exists.
☐ Enable MFA for the root user.
☐ Sign out of the root user.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The account has a dedicated non-root training user and the root user is no longer used for normal work.
consoleSteps.warning: Do not create root access keys. Do not share the root password or MFA device.

cliSteps.command: aws iam create-user --user-name fa-rds-alb-ec2-lab-user --profile <ADMIN_PROFILE>
cliSteps.explanation: Run as an existing administrator only. IAM is global, so this command intentionally has no --region. The command creates the dedicated lab user.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response contains UserName fa-rds-alb-ec2-lab-user.
cliSteps.warning: Do not run this command with root credentials.

verification.title: Confirm non-root access is available
verification.instruction: Sign in through the recorded IAM-user sign-in URL as fa-rds-alb-ec2-lab-user.
verification.expectedResult: The AWS console identifies the signed-in principal as the training IAM user.

verification.title: Confirm root safety
verification.instruction: Confirm that no root access key exists and that MFA protects the root user.
verification.expectedResult: Normal training work can proceed without root credentials.

tasks.title: Create and attach the scoped training policy
tasks.goal: Create fa-rds-alb-ec2-lab-policy and attach it to the training user before provisioning lab resources.
tasks.whyItMatters: A policy defines which actions an identity may perform. Some create operations require broad resource scope because the resource does not exist yet; later actions are narrowed to the named training resources where practical. The iam:PassRole statement is constrained to the EC2 Session Manager role and EC2 service.

consoleSteps.title: Create the training permissions policy
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The training user has permissions for the named lab and can pass only the named EC2 role to EC2.
consoleSteps.warning: This is a training policy, not a production policy. Remove it during final cleanup.

cliSteps.command: aws iam create-policy --policy-name fa-rds-alb-ec2-lab-policy --policy-document file://fa-rds-alb-ec2-lab-policy.json --profile <ADMIN_PROFILE>
cliSteps.explanation: Save the supplied policy JSON locally as fa-rds-alb-ec2-lab-policy.json after replacing <ACCOUNT_ID>. IAM is global, so no --region is used.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response contains the policy ARN.
cliSteps.warning: Use the JSON exactly as reviewed by the account administrator.

cliSteps.command: aws iam attach-user-policy --user-name fa-rds-alb-ec2-lab-user --policy-arn arn:aws:iam::<ACCOUNT_ID>:policy/fa-rds-alb-ec2-lab-policy --profile <ADMIN_PROFILE>
cliSteps.explanation: Replace <ACCOUNT_ID> with the account ID. This attaches the policy to only the named training user.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The policy is attached to fa-rds-alb-ec2-lab-user.
cliSteps.warning: IAM changes can take a short time to propagate.

verification.title: Confirm intended policy attachment
verification.instruction: Open the Permissions tab for fa-rds-alb-ec2-lab-user and inspect the attached policy.
verification.expectedResult: fa-rds-alb-ec2-lab-policy is attached to the dedicated user.

verification.title: Confirm PassRole scope
verification.instruction: Inspect the iam:PassRole statement in the policy.
verification.expectedResult: Only fa-rds-alb-ec2-ssm-role can be passed, and only to ec2.amazonaws.com.

tasks.title: Configure the named AWS CLI profile for eu-west-2
tasks.goal: Create the fa-rds-alb-ec2-lab profile and prove the caller identity before creating regional resources.
tasks.whyItMatters: Using a named profile prevents accidental use of another account or Region. eu-west-2 is Europe (London); all regional commands in this Follow Along explicitly use it.

consoleSteps.title: Create safe programmatic access

instructions.text: ☐ Delete the downloaded file after configuring the CLI.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: A temporary training access key is available only to configure the named local profile.
consoleSteps.warning: The secret access key is displayed only once. Never place it in source code, screenshots, user data, shell history, or notes.

cliSteps.command: aws configure --profile fa-rds-alb-ec2-lab
cliSteps.explanation: Enter the newly created IAM-user access key, secret access key, eu-west-2 as Default Region, and json as Default output format when prompted.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The local AWS CLI has the named profile.
cliSteps.warning: This interactive command writes credentials to the local shared credentials file.

cliSteps.command: aws sts get-caller-identity --profile fa-rds-alb-ec2-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Verify the account and ARN used by the training profile.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The result contains Account, Arn, and UserId for the training IAM user.
cliSteps.warning: Stop if the ARN is not the intended training identity.

verification.title: Confirm the active identity
verification.instruction: Inspect the Arn returned by get-caller-identity.
verification.expectedResult: The ARN identifies fa-rds-alb-ec2-lab-user rather than the root user.

verification.title: Confirm the Region
verification.instruction: Run subsequent regional CLI commands only with --region eu-west-2.
verification.expectedResult: Resources are created in Europe (London).

cleanup.title: Remove the local training profile
cleanup.instruction: After all AWS resource cleanup is complete, manually remove only the fa-rds-alb-ec2-lab profile from the local AWS CLI credentials and config files.
cleanup.description: After all AWS resource cleanup is complete, manually remove only the fa-rds-alb-ec2-lab profile from the local AWS CLI credentials and config files.
cleanup.verification: The named profile no longer appears in local AWS CLI configuration.

tasks.title: Create the dedicated VPC and six subnets
tasks.goal: Create fa-rds-alb-ec2-vpc with two public ALB subnets, two private application subnets, and two isolated database subnets across two Availability Zones.
tasks.whyItMatters: A public subnet has a route to an internet gateway. Private application subnets use NAT for outbound-only internet access. Database subnets intentionally have no direct default route to the internet. SAA-C03 questions commonly test these route-table distinctions.

consoleSteps.title: Create the VPC
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The dedicated VPC exists with DNS support enabled.
consoleSteps.warning: Do not use the default VPC for this Follow Along.

consoleSteps.title: Create the six tier subnets

instructions.text: ☐ Enable public IPv4 assignment for both public subnets only.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: Six named subnets exist in two Availability Zones with separate public, application, and database tiers.
consoleSteps.warning: Record every subnet ID from the Subnets list. Later commands use [PUBLIC_A_ID], [PUBLIC_B_ID], [APP_A_ID], [APP_B_ID], [DB_A_ID], and [DB_B_ID].

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 create-vpc --cidr-block 10.20.0.0/16 --tag-specifications ResourceType=vpc,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=fa-rds-alb-ec2-vpc}] --profile fa-rds-alb-ec2-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Record the returned VpcId as [VPC_ID].
cliSteps.expectedResult: A VPC with CIDR 10.20.0.0/16 is created.
cliSteps.warning: Use only the returned VPC ID in subsequent VPC commands.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 modify-vpc-attribute --vpc-id [VPC_ID] --enable-dns-support {"Value":true} --profile fa-rds-alb-ec2-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Enable DNS resolution for the training VPC.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The VPC accepts the DNS-support setting.
cliSteps.warning: Replace [VPC_ID] with the earlier create-vpc output.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 modify-vpc-attribute --vpc-id [VPC_ID] --enable-dns-hostnames {"Value":true} --profile fa-rds-alb-ec2-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Enable DNS hostnames for resources that need VPC DNS behavior.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The VPC accepts the DNS-hostnames setting.
cliSteps.warning: Replace [VPC_ID] with the earlier create-vpc output.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 create-subnet --vpc-id [VPC_ID] --availability-zone eu-west-2a --cidr-block 10.20.0.0/24 --tag-specifications ResourceType=subnet,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=fa-rds-alb-ec2-public-a}] --profile fa-rds-alb-ec2-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Record the returned SubnetId as [PUBLIC_A_ID].
cliSteps.expectedResult: The public-a subnet is created.
cliSteps.warning: Availability Zone names can be account mapped; use the Console path if eu-west-2a is unavailable in the account.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 create-subnet --vpc-id [VPC_ID] --availability-zone eu-west-2b --cidr-block 10.20.1.0/24 --tag-specifications ResourceType=subnet,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=fa-rds-alb-ec2-public-b}] --profile fa-rds-alb-ec2-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Record the returned SubnetId as [PUBLIC_B_ID].
cliSteps.expectedResult: The public-b subnet is created.
cliSteps.warning: Use a different Availability Zone from public-a.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 create-subnet --vpc-id [VPC_ID] --availability-zone eu-west-2a --cidr-block 10.20.10.0/24 --tag-specifications ResourceType=subnet,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=fa-rds-alb-ec2-app-a}] --profile fa-rds-alb-ec2-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Record the returned SubnetId as [APP_A_ID].
cliSteps.expectedResult: The app-a subnet is created.
cliSteps.warning: This subnet remains private.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 create-subnet --vpc-id [VPC_ID] --availability-zone eu-west-2b --cidr-block 10.20.11.0/24 --tag-specifications ResourceType=subnet,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=fa-rds-alb-ec2-app-b}] --profile fa-rds-alb-ec2-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Record the returned SubnetId as [APP_B_ID].
cliSteps.expectedResult: The app-b subnet is created.
cliSteps.warning: This subnet remains private.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 create-subnet --vpc-id [VPC_ID] --availability-zone eu-west-2a --cidr-block 10.20.20.0/24 --tag-specifications ResourceType=subnet,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=fa-rds-alb-ec2-db-a}] --profile fa-rds-alb-ec2-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Record the returned SubnetId as [DB_A_ID].
cliSteps.expectedResult: The db-a subnet is created.
cliSteps.warning: This subnet must have no direct internet route.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 create-subnet --vpc-id [VPC_ID] --availability-zone eu-west-2b --cidr-block 10.20.21.0/24 --tag-specifications ResourceType=subnet,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=fa-rds-alb-ec2-db-b}] --profile fa-rds-alb-ec2-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Record the returned SubnetId as [DB_B_ID].
cliSteps.expectedResult: The db-b subnet is created.
cliSteps.warning: This subnet must have no direct internet route.

verification.title: Confirm tier placement
verification.instruction: Inspect all six subnets and confirm two public, two app, and two database subnets span two Availability Zones.
verification.expectedResult: The intended three-tier topology exists before routing is configured.

verification.title: Confirm database isolation intent
verification.instruction: Confirm that the DB subnet CIDRs are separate from public and app subnet CIDRs.
verification.expectedResult: The database tier can remain isolated from direct internet routing.

tasks.title: Create internet, NAT, and route-table paths
tasks.goal: Create the public internet path, private application NAT path, and isolated database route table.
tasks.whyItMatters: Route tables decide where subnet traffic is sent. The NAT gateway allows private EC2 instances to obtain package updates without accepting unsolicited internet traffic. NAT gateways and Elastic IPs are chargeable; delete them promptly during cleanup.

consoleSteps.title: Create the public internet path
consoleSteps.expectedResult: Both public ALB subnets route IPv4 internet traffic through the internet gateway.
consoleSteps.warning: Only public ALB subnets receive this internet-gateway default route.

consoleSteps.title: Create the private application NAT path
consoleSteps.expectedResult: Private application subnets have outbound internet access through the NAT gateway.
consoleSteps.warning: A single NAT gateway is a cost-saving training design, not a multi-AZ NAT high-availability design.

consoleSteps.title: Create the isolated database route table

instructions.text: ☐ Do not add a default route.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: Database subnets use an isolated route table without a direct internet route.
consoleSteps.warning: Do not route database subnets to the internet gateway or NAT gateway for this lab.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 create-internet-gateway --tag-specifications ResourceType=internet-gateway,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=fa-rds-alb-ec2-igw}] --profile fa-rds-alb-ec2-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Record the returned InternetGatewayId as [IGW_ID].
cliSteps.expectedResult: The internet gateway is created.
cliSteps.warning: Attach it only to the training VPC.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 attach-internet-gateway --internet-gateway-id [IGW_ID] --vpc-id [VPC_ID] --profile fa-rds-alb-ec2-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Attach the new gateway to the training VPC.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The internet gateway is attached.
cliSteps.warning: Replace both IDs with outputs created in this Follow Along.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 create-route-table --vpc-id [VPC_ID] --tag-specifications ResourceType=route-table,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=fa-rds-alb-ec2-public-rt}] --profile fa-rds-alb-ec2-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Record the returned RouteTableId as [PUBLIC_RT_ID].
cliSteps.expectedResult: The public route table is created.
cliSteps.warning: This route table will be associated only with public subnets.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 create-route --route-table-id [PUBLIC_RT_ID] --destination-cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 --gateway-id [IGW_ID] --profile fa-rds-alb-ec2-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Create the public default route through the internet gateway.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The route table contains 0.0.0.0/0 to the IGW.
cliSteps.warning: Do not add this route to app or database route tables.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 allocate-address --domain vpc --profile fa-rds-alb-ec2-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Record the returned AllocationId as [EIP_ALLOCATION_ID].
cliSteps.expectedResult: An Elastic IP is allocated for the NAT gateway.
cliSteps.warning: An unassociated Elastic IP can incur charges.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 create-nat-gateway --subnet-id [PUBLIC_A_ID] --allocation-id [EIP_ALLOCATION_ID] --tag-specifications ResourceType=natgateway,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=fa-rds-alb-ec2-nat-a}] --profile fa-rds-alb-ec2-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Record the returned NatGatewayId as [NAT_ID], then wait for Available in the Console before adding routes.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The NAT gateway begins creating in the public-a subnet.
cliSteps.warning: NAT gateways incur hourly and data-processing charges.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 create-route-table --vpc-id [VPC_ID] --tag-specifications ResourceType=route-table,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=fa-rds-alb-ec2-app-rt}] --profile fa-rds-alb-ec2-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Record the returned RouteTableId as [APP_RT_ID].
cliSteps.expectedResult: The application route table is created.
cliSteps.warning: This route table is for private application subnets only.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 create-route --route-table-id [APP_RT_ID] --destination-cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 --nat-gateway-id [NAT_ID] --profile fa-rds-alb-ec2-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Create outbound-only internet routing for private application subnets.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The application route table contains 0.0.0.0/0 to the NAT gateway.
cliSteps.warning: The NAT gateway must be Available first.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 create-route-table --vpc-id [VPC_ID] --tag-specifications ResourceType=route-table,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=fa-rds-alb-ec2-db-rt}] --profile fa-rds-alb-ec2-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Record the returned RouteTableId as [DB_RT_ID].
cliSteps.expectedResult: The isolated database route table is created.
cliSteps.warning: Do not create a 0.0.0.0/0 route in this route table.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 associate-route-table --route-table-id [PUBLIC_RT_ID] --subnet-id [PUBLIC_A_ID] --profile fa-rds-alb-ec2-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Associate public-a with the public route table.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The association is returned.
cliSteps.warning: Repeat the equivalent supported Console action for public-b.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 associate-route-table --route-table-id [APP_RT_ID] --subnet-id [APP_A_ID] --profile fa-rds-alb-ec2-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Associate app-a with the application route table.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The association is returned.
cliSteps.warning: Repeat the equivalent supported Console action for app-b.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 associate-route-table --route-table-id [DB_RT_ID] --subnet-id [DB_A_ID] --profile fa-rds-alb-ec2-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Associate db-a with the isolated database route table.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The association is returned.
cliSteps.warning: Repeat the equivalent supported Console action for db-b.

verification.title: Confirm public subnet routing
verification.instruction: Inspect fa-rds-alb-ec2-public-rt and verify 0.0.0.0/0 targets fa-rds-alb-ec2-igw.
verification.expectedResult: The ALB subnets are public.

verification.title: Confirm private and isolated routing
verification.instruction: Inspect the application and database route tables.
verification.expectedResult: Application subnets route 0.0.0.0/0 to the NAT gateway, while database subnets have no default internet route.

tasks.title: Create the three security-group chain
tasks.goal: Create public ALB, protected EC2 web, and private RDS security groups with only the required inbound paths.
tasks.whyItMatters: Security groups are stateful and support security-group references. This allows the database to authorize the web tier by identity rather than by a changing private IP address. Network ACLs are subnet-level controls and are stateless.

consoleSteps.title: Create the public ALB security group

instructions.text: ☐ Record the security group ID as [ALB_SG_ID].

consoleSteps.expectedResult: Only the internet-facing ALB tier permits public HTTP.
consoleSteps.warning: Do not add this public rule to the web or RDS security group.

consoleSteps.title: Create the web and RDS security groups
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The web tier accepts HTTP only from the ALB, and RDS accepts MySQL only from the web tier.
consoleSteps.warning: Do not open SSH. Do not use 0.0.0.0/0 or an individual EC2 IP address for the RDS rule.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 create-security-group --group-name fa-rds-alb-ec2-alb-sg --description "Internet HTTP to ALB only" --vpc-id [VPC_ID] --profile fa-rds-alb-ec2-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Record the returned GroupId as [ALB_SG_ID].
cliSteps.expectedResult: The ALB security group is created.
cliSteps.warning: Security-group names must be unique in the VPC.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 authorize-security-group-ingress --group-id [ALB_SG_ID] --protocol tcp --port 80 --cidr 0.0.0.0/0 --profile fa-rds-alb-ec2-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Permit temporary public HTTP to the ALB tier only.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The ALB SG has inbound TCP 80 from 0.0.0.0/0.
cliSteps.warning: Do not reuse this public rule on backend tiers.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 create-security-group --group-name fa-rds-alb-ec2-web-sg --description "HTTP from ALB only" --vpc-id [VPC_ID] --profile fa-rds-alb-ec2-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Record the returned GroupId as [WEB_SG_ID].
cliSteps.expectedResult: The web security group is created.
cliSteps.warning: Keep the web and ALB security groups separate.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 authorize-security-group-ingress --group-id [WEB_SG_ID] --protocol tcp --port 80 --source-group [ALB_SG_ID] --profile fa-rds-alb-ec2-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Permit HTTP only when the source network interface uses the ALB security group.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The web SG references the ALB SG on TCP 80.
cliSteps.warning: This rule is stateful; response traffic is automatically allowed.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 create-security-group --group-name fa-rds-alb-ec2-rds-sg --description "MySQL from web tier only" --vpc-id [VPC_ID] --profile fa-rds-alb-ec2-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Record the returned GroupId as [RDS_SG_ID].
cliSteps.expectedResult: The RDS security group is created.
cliSteps.warning: Attach this group only to the RDS database.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 authorize-security-group-ingress --group-id [RDS_SG_ID] --protocol tcp --port 3306 --source-group [WEB_SG_ID] --profile fa-rds-alb-ec2-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Permit MySQL only from EC2 instances using the web security group.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The RDS SG references the web SG on TCP 3306.
cliSteps.warning: Network permission does not replace MySQL authentication.

verification.title: Verify the intended three-hop flow
verification.instruction: Inspect all inbound rules.
verification.expectedResult: The only intended inbound paths are internet → ALB TCP 80, ALB SG → web SG TCP 80, and web SG → RDS SG TCP 3306.

verification.title: Compare security groups and network ACLs
verification.instruction: State the difference between the two controls.
verification.expectedResult: Security groups are stateful resource-level firewalls; network ACLs are stateless subnet-level controls.

tasks.title: Create the Session Manager role and private web target A
tasks.feature: Amazon EC2 and AWS Systems Manager
tasks.goal: Create the EC2 instance role and instance profile, then launch fa-rds-alb-ec2-web-a in the private application subnet with web-server user data.
tasks.whyItMatters: Session Manager enables managed access without opening inbound SSH. The web server is private; users must reach it through the ALB rather than through a public IP.

consoleSteps.title: Create the EC2 Session Manager role

jsonBlocks.title: EC2 trust policy for CLI role creation
Web target A user data
jsonBlocks.content:
#!/bin/bash DNF_CMD=$(command -v dnf || command -v yum) $DNF_CMD install -y httpd mariadb105 || $DNF_CMD install -y httpd mariadb echo '

fa-rds-alb-ec2 web target A

' > /var/www/html/index.html systemctl enable --now httpd

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The EC2 role can register the instance with Systems Manager and the user data installs Apache HTTP Server.
consoleSteps.warning: Do not put credentials, secrets, database passwords, or endpoints in user data.

consoleSteps.title: Launch the private web target

instructions.text: ☐ Paste the web target A user data.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: A private EC2 instance starts in the application subnet and begins installing the web service through NAT.
consoleSteps.warning: If package installation fails, inspect the app subnet route table, NAT gateway status, and NAT Elastic IP association.

cliSteps.command: aws iam create-role --role-name fa-rds-alb-ec2-ssm-role --assume-role-policy-document file://ec2-trust-policy.json --profile fa-rds-alb-ec2-lab
cliSteps.explanation: Save the supplied trust JSON as ec2-trust-policy.json. IAM is global, so no --region is used.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response includes the role ARN.
cliSteps.warning: The trust policy must allow only ec2.amazonaws.com to assume the role.

cliSteps.command: aws iam attach-role-policy --role-name fa-rds-alb-ec2-ssm-role --policy-arn arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore --profile fa-rds-alb-ec2-lab
cliSteps.explanation: Attach the documented AWS managed policy to the EC2 role.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The role has the Session Manager managed policy.
cliSteps.warning: IAM is global, so no --region is used.

cliSteps.command: aws iam create-instance-profile --instance-profile-name fa-rds-alb-ec2-ssm-profile --profile fa-rds-alb-ec2-lab
cliSteps.explanation: Create the profile that EC2 can attach to the instance.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The instance profile is created.
cliSteps.warning: IAM is global, so no --region is used.

cliSteps.command: aws iam add-role-to-instance-profile --instance-profile-name fa-rds-alb-ec2-ssm-profile --role-name fa-rds-alb-ec2-ssm-role --profile fa-rds-alb-ec2-lab
cliSteps.explanation: Add the EC2 role to the instance profile.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The profile contains the named role.
cliSteps.warning: IAM is global, so no --region is used.

cliSteps.command: aws ssm get-parameter --name /aws/service/ami-amazon-linux-latest/al2023-ami-kernel-default-x86_64 --query Parameter.Value --output text --profile fa-rds-alb-ec2-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Record the returned AMI ID as [AL2023_AMI_ID].
cliSteps.expectedResult: A current regional Amazon Linux AMI ID is returned.
cliSteps.warning: Use an x86_64-compatible instance type.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 run-instances --image-id [AL2023_AMI_ID] --instance-type t3.micro --count 1 --subnet-id [APP_A_ID] --security-group-ids [WEB_SG_ID] --iam-instance-profile Name=fa-rds-alb-ec2-ssm-profile --user-data file://web-a-user-data.sh --tag-specifications ResourceType=instance,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=fa-rds-alb-ec2-web-a}] --profile fa-rds-alb-ec2-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Save the supplied user-data text as web-a-user-data.sh. Record the returned instance ID as [EC2_A_ID].
cliSteps.expectedResult: Target A begins in pending state.
cliSteps.warning: The caller requires the limited iam:PassRole permission created earlier.

verification.title: Confirm private instance placement
verification.instruction: Inspect target A networking and security groups.
verification.expectedResult: The instance is in app-a, has no public IPv4 address, and uses fa-rds-alb-ec2-web-sg.

verification.title: Confirm Systems Manager readiness
verification.instruction: Open Systems Manager Managed nodes and wait for target A to appear.
verification.expectedResult: Session Manager can access the private instance without an SSH rule.

tasks.title: Create the target group and internet-facing ALB
tasks.goal: Create fa-rds-alb-ec2-tg, register target A, create fa-rds-alb-ec2 across both public subnets, and create an HTTP listener.
tasks.whyItMatters: ALB is a Layer 7 load balancer. SAA-C03 phrases such as HTTP-aware routing, host-based routing, path-based routing, and a single public web endpoint indicate ALB rather than direct EC2 access or a Network Load Balancer.

consoleSteps.title: Create the HTTP target group
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The target group registers target A on port 80.
consoleSteps.warning: The target becomes healthy only after user data finishes and the ALB can reach port 80.

consoleSteps.title: Create the ALB and listener

instructions.text: ☐ Create an HTTP listener on port 80.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The ALB has an HTTP listener forwarding its default action to the target group.
consoleSteps.warning: HTTP is for this temporary training validation. Production internet-facing applications normally use HTTPS and an appropriate certificate.

cliSteps.command: aws elbv2 create-target-group --name fa-rds-alb-ec2-tg --protocol HTTP --port 80 --target-type instance --health-check-path / --vpc-id [VPC_ID] --profile fa-rds-alb-ec2-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Record TargetGroupArn as [TARGET_GROUP_ARN].
cliSteps.expectedResult: The HTTP instance target group is created.
cliSteps.warning: The target-group name must be unique in the Region.

cliSteps.command: aws elbv2 register-targets --target-group-arn [TARGET_GROUP_ARN] --targets Id=[EC2_A_ID],Port=80 --profile fa-rds-alb-ec2-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Register web target A on port 80.
cliSteps.expectedResult: Target A is registered.
cliSteps.warning: Registration does not mean health checks have passed.

cliSteps.command: aws elbv2 create-load-balancer --name fa-rds-alb-ec2 --type application --scheme internet-facing --ip-address-type ipv4 --subnets [PUBLIC_A_ID] [PUBLIC_B_ID] --security-groups [ALB_SG_ID] --profile fa-rds-alb-ec2-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Record LoadBalancerArn as [ALB_ARN] and DNSName as [ALB_DNS_NAME].
cliSteps.expectedResult: An internet-facing ALB begins provisioning in two Availability Zones.
cliSteps.warning: The ALB requires subnets in at least two Availability Zones.

cliSteps.command: aws elbv2 create-listener --load-balancer-arn [ALB_ARN] --protocol HTTP --port 80 --default-actions Type=forward,TargetGroupArn=[TARGET_GROUP_ARN] --profile fa-rds-alb-ec2-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Record the returned ListenerArn as [LISTENER_ARN].
cliSteps.expectedResult: The HTTP listener forwards to the target group.
cliSteps.warning: Use HTTPS for production traffic.

verification.title: Confirm target health
verification.instruction: Open the Targets tab for fa-rds-alb-ec2-tg and wait for target A to be Healthy.
verification.expectedResult: The ALB can reach the private EC2 web server through the security-group reference.

verification.title: Confirm public entry point
verification.instruction: Open http://[ALB_DNS_NAME] in a browser.
verification.expectedResult: The browser displays the target A page through the ALB.

tasks.title: Add target B and practice registration and graceful deregistration
tasks.goal: Launch target B in the second application Availability Zone, register it, observe traffic capacity, and safely deregister target A.
tasks.whyItMatters: Two healthy targets in different Availability Zones improve web-tier resilience. ALB cross-zone load balancing is always enabled. In production, use EC2 Auto Scaling to replace unhealthy or failed instances automatically rather than manually launching replacements.

consoleSteps.title: Launch and register target B

instructions.text: ☐ Select the same Amazon Linux AMI.
☐ Paste the target B user data.

jsonBlocks.title: Web target B user data
jsonBlocks.content:
#!/bin/bash DNF_CMD=$(command -v dnf || command -v yum) $DNF_CMD install -y httpd mariadb105 || $DNF_CMD install -y httpd mariadb echo '

fa-rds-alb-ec2 web target B

' > /var/www/html/index.html systemctl enable --now httpd

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The target group has healthy targets in app-a and app-b.
consoleSteps.warning: Do not add a public inbound rule to target B.

consoleSteps.title: Practice graceful deregistration
consoleSteps.expectedResult: Target B continues serving requests while target A drains, then target A returns to the healthy pool.
consoleSteps.warning: Deregistering a target does not terminate its EC2 instance.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 run-instances --image-id [AL2023_AMI_ID] --instance-type t3.micro --count 1 --subnet-id [APP_B_ID] --security-group-ids [WEB_SG_ID] --iam-instance-profile Name=fa-rds-alb-ec2-ssm-profile --user-data file://web-b-user-data.sh --tag-specifications ResourceType=instance,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=fa-rds-alb-ec2-web-b}] --profile fa-rds-alb-ec2-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Save the supplied target B user data as web-b-user-data.sh and record the returned instance ID as [EC2_B_ID].
cliSteps.expectedResult: Target B begins launching in app-b.
cliSteps.warning: Use the second application subnet.

cliSteps.command: aws elbv2 register-targets --target-group-arn [TARGET_GROUP_ARN] --targets Id=[EC2_B_ID],Port=80 --profile fa-rds-alb-ec2-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Register target B on port 80.
cliSteps.expectedResult: Target B is registered and later becomes healthy.
cliSteps.warning: Wait for health checks before testing traffic distribution.

cliSteps.command: aws elbv2 modify-target-group-attributes --target-group-arn [TARGET_GROUP_ARN] --attributes Key=deregistration_delay.timeout_seconds,Value=60 --profile fa-rds-alb-ec2-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Set an observable 60-second draining period for this lab.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The target-group deregistration delay is updated.
cliSteps.warning: Use an application-appropriate delay in production.

cliSteps.command: aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn [TARGET_GROUP_ARN] --targets Id=[EC2_A_ID],Port=80 --profile fa-rds-alb-ec2-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Begin graceful deregistration of target A.
cliSteps.expectedResult: Target A enters draining and then unused state.
cliSteps.warning: Re-register target A after this observation so later failure labs have two targets.

cliSteps.command: aws elbv2 register-targets --target-group-arn [TARGET_GROUP_ARN] --targets Id=[EC2_A_ID],Port=80 --profile fa-rds-alb-ec2-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Restore target A to the known working target pool.
cliSteps.expectedResult: Target A later becomes healthy again.
cliSteps.warning: Wait for health checks to complete.

verification.title: Confirm multi-AZ web capacity
verification.instruction: Confirm both targets are Healthy and located in different application subnets.
verification.expectedResult: The ALB can route requests to healthy targets across two Availability Zones.

verification.title: Confirm graceful target removal
verification.instruction: Confirm that target A enters Draining after deregistration while target B remains Healthy.
verification.expectedResult: The learner distinguishes deregistration from instance termination.

tasks.title: Create the DB subnet group and private RDS for MySQL database
tasks.goal: Create fa-rds-alb-ec2-db-subnets and a non-public MySQL DB instance in isolated database subnets.
tasks.whyItMatters: A DB subnet group spans Availability Zones and permits later Multi-AZ deployment. Private database placement plus a security-group reference implements least-privilege network access. Multi-AZ provides availability and failover; read replicas provide read scaling.

consoleSteps.title: Create the DB subnet group
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The DB subnet group includes private database subnets in two Availability Zones.
consoleSteps.warning: Do not include public or application subnets in the DB subnet group.

consoleSteps.title: Create the private MySQL DB instance

instructions.text: ☐ Select a supported current MySQL version.
☐ Set DB instance identifier to fa-rds-alb-ec2-db.
☐ Set initial database name to appdb.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: A private RDS for MySQL DB instance becomes Available with one day of automated backups.
consoleSteps.warning: RDS instances, storage, automated backups beyond included allowance, and manual snapshots can incur charges. Do not expose the DB publicly.

cliSteps.command: aws rds create-db-subnet-group --db-subnet-group-name fa-rds-alb-ec2-db-subnets --db-subnet-group-description "Private database subnets for RDS ALB EC2 lab" --subnet-ids [DB_A_ID] [DB_B_ID] --profile fa-rds-alb-ec2-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Create the DB subnet group from the two earlier database subnet IDs.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response contains DBSubnetGroupName fa-rds-alb-ec2-db-subnets.
cliSteps.warning: The subnets must be in different Availability Zones.

cliSteps.command: aws rds create-db-instance --db-instance-identifier fa-rds-alb-ec2-db --db-name appdb --allocated-storage 20 --db-instance-class db.t3.micro --engine mysql --master-username appadmin --manage-master-user-password --vpc-security-group-ids [RDS_SG_ID] --db-subnet-group-name fa-rds-alb-ec2-db-subnets --backup-retention-period 1 --no-publicly-accessible --no-multi-az --profile fa-rds-alb-ec2-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Create the initial Single-AZ private database while allowing RDS to manage the master password in Secrets Manager.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The DB instance begins in creating state.
cliSteps.warning: Confirm db.t3.micro is available for the selected MySQL engine in eu-west-2 before running.

cliSteps.command: aws rds wait db-instance-available --db-instance-identifier fa-rds-alb-ec2-db --profile fa-rds-alb-ec2-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Wait until the database becomes Available.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The waiter returns after the DB instance is available.
cliSteps.warning: The database can take several minutes to create.

cliSteps.command: aws rds describe-db-instances --db-instance-identifier fa-rds-alb-ec2-db --query DBInstances[0].{Endpoint:Endpoint.Address,Port:Endpoint.Port,Public:PubliclyAccessible,Status:DBInstanceStatus,MultiAZ:MultiAZ,BackupRetention:BackupRetentionPeriod} --output table --profile fa-rds-alb-ec2-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Record Endpoint as [RDS_ENDPOINT].
cliSteps.expectedResult: The table shows Available, Public false, port 3306, MultiAZ false, and backup retention 1.
cliSteps.warning: Treat the private endpoint as internal infrastructure information.

verification.title: Confirm private database placement
verification.instruction: Inspect the RDS Connectivity and security section.
verification.expectedResult: Publicly accessible is false, the DB subnet group is fa-rds-alb-ec2-db-subnets, and the attached security group is fa-rds-alb-ec2-rds-sg.

verification.title: Apply the high-availability decision
verification.instruction: Compare Multi-AZ and read replicas.
verification.expectedResult: Multi-AZ is selected for automatic failover and availability; read replicas are selected for read scaling.

tasks.title: Validate private EC2-to-RDS connectivity and separate failure layers
tasks.goal: Use Session Manager to connect from EC2 to RDS, then distinguish DNS, network, port, and database-authentication failures.
tasks.whyItMatters: A timeout usually indicates routing, subnet placement, security-group, port, NAT, or endpoint-path trouble. Access denied indicates database authentication trouble. Name-resolution errors suggest DNS or endpoint errors. SAA-C03 troubleshooting requires identifying the narrowest failed layer.

consoleSteps.title: Connect from the private web target

instructions.text: ☐ Retrieve the managed secret through the approved console path.
☐ Enter the password only at the password prompt.

jsonBlocks.title: MySQL command for the Session Manager shell

consoleSteps.expectedResult: SELECT 1 returns a result, proving both EC2-to-RDS network access and valid MySQL authentication.
consoleSteps.warning: Never place the database password in commands, shell history, user data, source code, screenshots, or notes.

consoleSteps.title: Practice and restore an RDS security-group failure

instructions.text: ☐ Remove the MySQL rule from fa-rds-alb-ec2-web-sg.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The connection fails while the security-group reference is absent and succeeds after the exact original rule is restored.
consoleSteps.warning: Do not make the database public and do not replace the source security group with an EC2 IP address.

cliSteps.command: aws ssm start-session --target [EC2_A_ID] --profile fa-rds-alb-ec2-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Open an interactive Session Manager shell on target A, then run the supplied MySQL client command inside that shell.
cliSteps.expectedResult: A Session Manager shell opens.
cliSteps.warning: If this fails, check the instance profile, managed-node status, app-subnet NAT route, and NAT gateway status before considering any network change.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 revoke-security-group-ingress --group-id [RDS_SG_ID] --protocol tcp --port 3306 --source-group [WEB_SG_ID] --profile fa-rds-alb-ec2-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Temporarily remove the known-working EC2-to-RDS network authorization.
cliSteps.expectedResult: A subsequent MySQL connection attempt cannot reach the database network path.
cliSteps.warning: Restore the rule immediately after observing the failure.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 authorize-security-group-ingress --group-id [RDS_SG_ID] --protocol tcp --port 3306 --source-group [WEB_SG_ID] --profile fa-rds-alb-ec2-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Restore the exact baseline RDS inbound rule.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The web tier can again reach TCP 3306.
cliSteps.warning: Correct network access still requires valid MySQL credentials.

verification.title: Prove the private database chain
verification.instruction: From Session Manager on target A, connect to [RDS_ENDPOINT] and run SELECT 1.
verification.expectedResult: The EC2 web security group is authorized to reach the private RDS security group on port 3306.

verification.title: Classify connection errors
verification.instruction: Deliberately use an invalid password after the network rule is restored.
verification.expectedResult: The database returns an authentication failure rather than a network timeout, demonstrating the difference between connectivity and authentication.

tasks.title: Monitor the architecture and create a manual recovery snapshot
tasks.feature: Amazon CloudWatch and Amazon RDS backups
tasks.goal: Inspect EC2, ALB, and RDS metrics, create a no-action healthy-host alarm, and create one manual RDS snapshot.
tasks.whyItMatters: CloudWatch shows availability and capacity signals. RDS automated backups support point-in-time recovery during the retention period; manual snapshots persist until explicitly deleted. These are distinct recovery mechanisms tested in SAA-C03.

consoleSteps.title: Inspect useful metrics

instructions.text: ☐ View EC2 CPUUtilization for web target A.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The learner can inspect compute, load-balancer availability, and database connection signals.
consoleSteps.warning: Low traffic can legitimately produce low or zero values in a training environment.

consoleSteps.title: Create an alarm and manual snapshot

instructions.text: ☐ Select the ALB and target-group dimensions.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: A no-action alarm exists and the manual snapshot becomes Available.
consoleSteps.warning: Manual snapshots can continue incurring storage charges until deleted.

cliSteps.command: aws cloudwatch put-metric-alarm --alarm-name fa-rds-alb-ec2-low-healthy-hosts --alarm-description "Training alarm for ALB healthy hosts" --namespace AWS/ApplicationELB --metric-name HealthyHostCount --dimensions Name=TargetGroup,Value=[TARGET_GROUP_DIMENSION] Name=LoadBalancer,Value=[LOAD_BALANCER_DIMENSION] --statistic Minimum --period 60 --evaluation-periods 1 --threshold 1 --comparison-operator LessThanThreshold --treat-missing-data breaching --profile fa-rds-alb-ec2-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Replace both dimensions with the exact values shown by CloudWatch for the existing ALB and target group. This creates no alarm action.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The named CloudWatch alarm is created.
cliSteps.warning: The dimensions must exactly match the existing resources.

cliSteps.command: aws rds create-db-snapshot --db-instance-identifier fa-rds-alb-ec2-db --db-snapshot-identifier fa-rds-alb-ec2-db-snap-001 --profile fa-rds-alb-ec2-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Create the manual recovery snapshot.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The snapshot begins in creating state.
cliSteps.warning: Manual snapshots persist after DB deletion until explicitly removed.

cliSteps.command: aws rds describe-db-snapshots --db-snapshot-identifier fa-rds-alb-ec2-db-snap-001 --query DBSnapshots[0].Status --output text --profile fa-rds-alb-ec2-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Repeat only after time has passed until the status is available.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The output becomes available.
cliSteps.warning: Do not delete the snapshot until final cleanup if you want to inspect it.

verification.title: Confirm baseline observability
verification.instruction: Inspect EC2 CPUUtilization, ALB HealthyHostCount, and RDS DatabaseConnections.
verification.expectedResult: The learner has visibility into each architecture tier.

verification.title: Confirm recoverability artifacts
verification.instruction: Inspect the alarm and manual snapshot.
verification.expectedResult: The named alarm exists and fa-rds-alb-ec2-db-snap-001 is Available.

cleanup.title: Delete the no-action alarm
cleanup.instruction: Delete only fa-rds-alb-ec2-low-healthy-hosts after the monitoring exercise.
cleanup.description: Delete only fa-rds-alb-ec2-low-healthy-hosts after the monitoring exercise.
cleanup.verification: The named alarm no longer appears in CloudWatch Alarms.

tasks.title: Practice controlled ALB failures and restore the baseline
tasks.goal: Create an incorrect health-check path and a blocked ALB-to-EC2 rule, observe evidence, and restore the exact working baseline.
tasks.whyItMatters: ALB sends traffic only to healthy registered targets. A wrong health-check path commonly produces response-code mismatch; a missing ALB-to-web security-group rule commonly causes a timeout. These are different failure layers.

consoleSteps.title: Test and restore an incorrect health-check path
consoleSteps.expectedResult: Targets become unhealthy with the wrong path and recover after / is restored.
consoleSteps.warning: Do not leave the target group configured with /missing.

consoleSteps.title: Test and restore blocked ALB-to-web traffic
consoleSteps.expectedResult: Removing the ALB-source rule blocks health checks, and restoring the exact security-group reference repairs the path.
consoleSteps.warning: Do not replace the ALB source group with 0.0.0.0/0.

cliSteps.command: aws elbv2 modify-target-group --target-group-arn [TARGET_GROUP_ARN] --health-check-path /missing --profile fa-rds-alb-ec2-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Temporarily set a path that the simple web page does not serve.
cliSteps.expectedResult: Targets later report unhealthy health-check evidence.
cliSteps.warning: Run the restoration command after observing the failure.

cliSteps.command: aws elbv2 modify-target-group --target-group-arn [TARGET_GROUP_ARN] --health-check-path / --profile fa-rds-alb-ec2-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Restore the known working health-check path.
cliSteps.expectedResult: Targets can return to healthy after successful checks.
cliSteps.warning: Recovery requires the configured healthy threshold.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 revoke-security-group-ingress --group-id [WEB_SG_ID] --protocol tcp --port 80 --source-group [ALB_SG_ID] --profile fa-rds-alb-ec2-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Temporarily remove ALB-to-web HTTP authorization.
cliSteps.expectedResult: Health checks later fail to reach the web targets.
cliSteps.warning: Restore this rule immediately after observing the failure.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 authorize-security-group-ingress --group-id [WEB_SG_ID] --protocol tcp --port 80 --source-group [ALB_SG_ID] --profile fa-rds-alb-ec2-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Restore the original ALB-to-web security-group reference.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The web tier again permits HTTP only from the ALB group.
cliSteps.warning: Do not broaden the rule to a public CIDR.

verification.title: Classify target-health evidence
verification.instruction: Compare the target health reason after the invalid path with the reason after the missing web security-group rule.
verification.expectedResult: The learner can distinguish application response failures from network reachability failures.

verification.title: Confirm known working baseline
verification.instruction: Confirm health-check path is / and both target A and target B are Healthy.
verification.expectedResult: The ALB environment is restored before final cleanup.

tasks.title: Apply SAA-C03 architecture decisions
tasks.goal: Map common exam wording to the correct load-balancing, database, availability, scaling, and connection-management choice.
tasks.whyItMatters: SAA-C03 tests requirement-driven decisions. Choose the service pattern that directly meets the availability, protocol, scaling, security, and operational requirement rather than choosing a familiar service by default.

consoleSteps.title: Review the architecture decisions

instructions.text: ☐ Open the RDS DB instance configuration.
☐ Review the Create read replica option.
☐ Record the purpose of Auto Scaling.
☐ Record the purpose of RDS Proxy.
☐ Record the purpose of Network Load Balancer.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The learner can connect requirement wording to the appropriate architecture component.
consoleSteps.warning: Do not enable Multi-AZ or create a read replica solely for review without approval for the additional cost and change.

cliSteps.command: aws rds describe-db-instances --db-instance-identifier fa-rds-alb-ec2-db --query DBInstances[0].{MultiAZ:MultiAZ,ReadReplicas:ReadReplicaDBInstanceIdentifiers,BackupRetention:BackupRetentionPeriod,StorageType:StorageType} --output table --profile fa-rds-alb-ec2-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Inspect the current Single-AZ, no-read-replica baseline without modifying the database.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The output shows the initial availability and read-scale state.
cliSteps.warning: This command does not create a standby or replica.

verification.title: State the SAA-C03 selection cues
verification.instruction: Explain the correct choice for each requirement.
verification.expectedResult: ALB: Layer 7 HTTP routing; NLB: Layer 4 TCP/UDP/TLS or static IP; direct EC2: not preferred for resilient public web entry; Auto Scaling: automatic instance replacement and scale-out; Multi-AZ: failover; read replica: read scaling; RDS Proxy: connection pooling and connection management; Aurora: managed relational alternative; private DB subnets plus SG references: least-privilege database access.

tasks.title: Perform reverse-dependency cleanup
tasks.goal: Remove only resources created by this Follow Along in a safe order, including chargeable networking, compute, load-balancing, database, backup, IAM, and local CLI resources.
tasks.whyItMatters: Deleting in reverse dependency order prevents resource-in-use errors and stops charges. Never delete resources that were not created by this Follow Along.

consoleSteps.title: Delete application and database resources
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The load balancer, targets, instances, DB instance, manual snapshot, alarm, and DB subnet group are removed.
consoleSteps.warning: A manual snapshot survives DB deletion unless you explicitly delete it.

consoleSteps.title: Delete networking, IAM, and local access resources

instructions.text: ☐ Remove fa-rds-alb-ec2-ssm-role from its instance profile.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: Only the dedicated Follow Along resources are removed and no chargeable lab resources remain.
consoleSteps.warning: Delete security groups only after dependent ALB, EC2, and RDS network interfaces are gone. Delete the NAT gateway before releasing its Elastic IP.

cliSteps.command: aws elbv2 delete-load-balancer --load-balancer-arn [ALB_ARN] --profile fa-rds-alb-ec2-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Delete only the ALB created by this Follow Along.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The ALB enters deletion.
cliSteps.warning: Delete the target group only after ALB deletion completes.

cliSteps.command: aws rds delete-db-instance --db-instance-identifier fa-rds-alb-ec2-db --skip-final-snapshot --delete-automated-backups --profile fa-rds-alb-ec2-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Delete only the training DB instance without creating an additional final snapshot.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The DB instance enters deleting state.
cliSteps.warning: This is destructive. The separately created manual snapshot remains until deleted.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 delete-nat-gateway --nat-gateway-id [NAT_ID] --profile fa-rds-alb-ec2-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Delete the training NAT gateway before releasing its Elastic IP.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The NAT gateway enters deleting state.
cliSteps.warning: Wait until deletion completes before deleting the VPC.

verification.title: Confirm no chargeable lab resources remain
verification.instruction: Inspect RDS Databases and Snapshots, EC2 Instances, NAT Gateways, Elastic IPs, Load Balancers, Target Groups, CloudWatch Alarms, and VPCs in eu-west-2.
verification.expectedResult: No resource beginning fa-rds-alb-ec2 remains.

verification.title: Confirm identity cleanup
verification.instruction: Inspect IAM users, policies, roles, and instance profiles, then inspect local AWS CLI profiles.
verification.expectedResult: The dedicated training user, policy, role, profile, access key, and local CLI profile no longer exist.

warnings.cost: NAT gateways, Elastic IP addresses, EC2 instances, Application Load Balancers, RDS DB instances, database storage, backup storage, manual snapshots, and data transfer can incur charges. Create resources only for the duration of the lab and complete the final cleanup promptly.
warnings.safety: Only the temporary internet-facing ALB allows inbound HTTP from 0.0.0.0/0. EC2 web targets have no public IP and accept HTTP only from the ALB security group. RDS is not publicly accessible and accepts MySQL only from the web security group. Use HTTPS and an ACM certificate for production internet-facing applications.
warnings.credentials: Never create root access keys. Never include access keys, secret access keys, session tokens, passwords, private keys, or database secret values in commands, user data, source code, screenshots, browser pages, or notes. Enter the RDS password only at the MySQL password prompt.
warnings.region: Use Europe (London), eu-west-2, throughout. IAM and STS commands are global and intentionally omit --region; every regional AWS CLI command includes --region eu-west-2.

findings.message: The supplied published source revision is 4. This replacement preserves the exact programme identity rds-learning-path and display name RDS, EC2, and Application Load Balancer Follow Along.
Availability Zone letters are account-mapped. The Console path lets the learner select two distinct eu-west-2 Availability Zones if eu-west-2a or eu-west-2b is unavailable in the account.

The scoped training policy uses broad service actions for disposable lab resources because several create operations do not yet have resource ARNs. An account administrator should review it against organizational SCPs, permissions boundaries, and service-control requirements before attachment.

The task uses one NAT gateway in one Availability Zone to reduce training cost. For production fault tolerance, use a NAT gateway in each Availability Zone and route each private subnet to its local NAT gateway.

Current DB engine versions and instance-class availability can vary by account and Region. The learner must confirm a supported MySQL version and db.t3.micro availability in eu-west-2 before creating the DB instance.
